name: Bar basics
credits: Bar basics: general UK bar practice and law, written by Claude. Venue drinks and glassware come from your official sheet.

stages.name: General UK bar rules (venue sheet to come)

notes.q: Glass for a pint of lager, bitter or cider?
notes.a: Pint glass (568 ml)

notes.q: Glass for a spirit and mixer (vodka & coke, rum & coke)?
notes.a: Highball: tall and straight
notes.note: Ice first, then the spirit, then the mixer.

notes.q: Glass for a spirit neat or on the rocks?
notes.a: Rocks glass (short tumbler)

notes.q: Glass for prosecco or champagne?
notes.a: Flute
notes.note: Tall and narrow so it keeps its bubbles.

notes.q: Glass for a G&T “served fancy”?
notes.a: Copa / balloon glass
notes.note: A highball is fine too unless your bar says otherwise.

notes.q: Glass for red, white or rosé?
notes.a: Wine glass, filled to the line for the size ordered

notes.q: Glass for a shot?
notes.a: Shot glass

notes.q: Before you hand over any glass, check…
notes.a: It’s clean, dry and not chipped or cracked
notes.note: A chipped glass goes straight to the bin, not back in the rack.

notes.q: Why are most stadium drinks served in plastic?
notes.a: Safety: no glass in crowds
notes.note: Use what your bar gives you; never carry glass onto the concourse.

notes.q: How many ml is a pint?
notes.a: 568 ml

notes.q: Sizes draught beer and cider can be sold in?
notes.a: ⅓, ½ or ⅔ pint, or multiples of ½ pint

notes.q: Legal single spirit measures (gin, vodka, rum, whisky)?
notes.a: 25 ml or 35 ml: the bar picks one and must display it

notes.q: A double at a 25 ml bar is…
notes.a: 50 ml

notes.q: Wine by the glass: legal sizes?
notes.a: 125 ml, 175 ml, or multiples (250 ml = large)
notes.note: A 125 ml glass must always be available, and customers told so.

notes.q: How many 250 ml glasses in a 750 ml bottle?
How many 125 ml glasses in a 750 ml bottle?
Pouring spirits: how?
notes.a: Always with a measure (optic or jigger), never free-poured

notes.q: Pouring a pint: how do you start?
notes.a: Glass at about 45°, beer aimed at the side

notes.q: Pouring a pint: how do you finish?
notes.a: Straighten the glass as it fills to build a small head

notes.q: Should the tap touch the beer or the glass?
notes.a: No: keep the nozzle out of the drink

notes.q: Guinness: how is it poured?
notes.a: Two parts: fill about ¾ at 45°, let it settle, then top up
notes.note: Don’t hand it over until it’s settled dark.

notes.q: Beer comes out as all foam (fobbing). Likely causes?
notes.a: Keg running out, a warm or dirty glass, or a gas/line problem
notes.note: Tell the cellar team; don’t keep pouring foam away.

notes.q: Beer spits and sputters from the tap?
notes.a: The keg is probably empty: call cellar to change it

notes.q: A shandy is…
notes.a: Beer topped with lemonade, roughly half and half

notes.q: A “lager top” is…
notes.a: A pint of lager with a splash of lemonade on top

notes.q: “With black” (e.g. cider and black) means…
notes.a: A dash of blackcurrant cordial

notes.q: Lager vs ale vs stout?
notes.a: Lager: pale, cold, fizzy. Ale/bitter: amber, less fizzy. Stout: dark and roasted (e.g. Guinness).

notes.q: Usual mixer for gin?
notes.a: Tonic (slimline if asked)

notes.q: Usual mixers for vodka?
notes.a: Coke, lemonade, cranberry or orange

notes.q: Which wines are served chilled?
notes.a: White, rosé and prosecco. Red at room temperature.

notes.q: Premixed cocktail: what do you do?
notes.a: Shake or stir it if your bar says to, pour into the right glass, garnish
notes.note: Your training said cocktails are premixed: no measuring needed.

notes.q: Legal age to buy alcohol in the UK?
Challenge 25 means…
notes.a: Ask for ID from anyone who looks under 25

notes.q: ID usually accepted?
notes.a: Passport, photo driving licence, or a PASS card (hologram)
notes.note: Check your venue’s list; no ID means no alcohol.

notes.q: Someone buying for a friend who looks under 18?
notes.a: Refuse: that’s a proxy sale and it’s illegal

notes.q: Can you serve someone who is clearly drunk?
notes.a: No: it’s an offence for you as well as the venue
notes.note: Refuse calmly, offer water or a soft drink, and tell your team leader.

notes.q: Refusing a sale: how?
notes.a: Polite, short, no arguing. “Sorry, I can’t serve you.” Get your team leader if it escalates.

notes.q: Can fans take alcohol to their seats in view of the pitch?
notes.a: No: in England and Wales it’s banned in view of the pitch during the match

notes.q: A customer asks what’s in a drink because of an allergy?
notes.a: Don’t guess: check the allergen sheet or ask your supervisor
notes.note: Beer has gluten; wine and many ciders have sulphites.

notes.q: Broken glass behind the bar?
notes.a: Stop serving in that spot, warn others, use a dustpan and brush, never hands

notes.q: Spill on the floor?
notes.a: Wet floor sign, then clean it straight away

notes.q: Quiet moment during service: what should you do?
notes.a: Clean as you go: wipe the bar, empty drip trays, restock

notes.q: £13.40 paid with a £20: change?
£8.75 paid with a £10: change?
Three drinks at £5.80 each: total?
